Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
903 AM EDT Mon Sep 7 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No changes have been made to the forecast this morning.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Dry and seasonable conditions with lower humidity early
  this week.

- 2) Shower & thunderstorm chances return midweek.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry and seasonable conditions with lower humidity
early this week.

High pressure will build into the region through Tuesday. Lower
humidity, dry conditions and sunshine with light winds will be 
expected during this period. The high moves to the western 
Atlantic just offshore of the East Coast Tuesday night. This 
will allow for a south to southwesterly flow to develop and 
continue through Wednesday. Warmth and humidity will begin to 
increase once again. High temperatures today will be in the low 
80s, accompanied by overnight lows in the 50s and low 60s. High 
temperatures Tuesday should reach the middle 80s, then into the 
upper 80s by Wednesday.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Shower & thunderstorm chances return midweek.

Surface high pressure begins to slide offshore on Wednesday. 
Temperatures & humidity increase somewhat during this time, with 
temperatures reaching the upper 80s and lower 90s by Thursday. 
Meanwhile, an upper-level trough centered over the Hudson Bay will 
produce a stemming cold front that tracks across the East Coast 
sometime mid-to-late week. Current guidance has widespread 
precipitation potential pinpointed for Thursday afternoon and 
evening as this frontal boundary tracks through. The 18z guidance 
remains a bit uncertain regarding exact timing for this, as the 
ECMWF is starting to slide later in the week. Regardless, showers & 
thunderstorms could occur as this front slides offshore towards the 
end of the week. The severe threat continues to look marginal right 
now , but some model guidance is starting to show a possibility for 
a couple of stronger storms given the increased heat & humidity at 
this point combined with potential wind shear. 

Temperatures drop again in the wake of the front late in the week, 
with conditions becoming much drier looking towards the weekend as 
high pressure moves in overhead.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
VFR conditions should persist through Wednesday night given the
general influence of high pressure over or near the region. 
This high pressure does depart by Tuesday which yields a return
of south to southwesterly flow. 

Showers & thunderstorms from an incoming cold front could bring 
reduced conditions at terminals on Thursday. Winds gusting up to 20-
25 knots are possible throughout the day before diminishing 
overnight. Conditions likely improve by Friday as southwesterly 
winds shift northeasterly.

&&

.MARINE...
No marine hazards are expected through Wednesday. Light flow is
expected, although gusts could creep up to 10 to 15 knots at times.
Northeasterly winds today shift southerly Tuesday, remaining below
SCA levels.

SCAs are likely beginning Wednesday night through Thursday as a cold 
front tracks over the region. Gusts up to 25 knots are possible,
with a few showers & thunderstorms possible over the waters 
during this period. Winds diminish by Friday afternoon in the 
wake of the front. Southwest winds shift northeasterly on 
Friday.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies remain elevated over the next several days due
to an onshore flow. Annapolis could reach minor tidal flooding a
few more times this week, other than early this morning during
high tide. Some other sensitive places could push Action stage.
